chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever takes hold of one corner of the coffin, Allah will forgive him twenty-five major sins, and when he takes hold of four (corners), he will be released from sins.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for carrying a coffin in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the tangible spiritual merit of participating in funeral rites, linking physical service to the deceased with divine mercy. The distinction between holding one corner (qaymah) versus all four (rubu') illustrates a graduated reward system, where greater effort yields complete absolution from major sins, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity and honoring the dead.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who grabs by a corner of the coffin, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive twenty five major sins for him, and when (he grabs) four (corners), he would exit from the sins’.
en.sarwar: 2. AI-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ishaq from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Sulayman ibn Khafid from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if one holds the corner of the coffin, Allah forgives his twenty- five major sins; and if he lifts up all four corners (at different times) he comes out of all sins.”
